examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{風|かぜ}が{強|つよ}いです。
{涼|すず}しい{風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}いています。
{風|かぜ}が{止|と}まったので、{外|そと}に{出|で}ました。
examples.english: The wind stopped, so I went outside.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}の{風|かぜ}は{気持|きも}ちがいいので、{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けて{部屋|へや}に{入|い}れましょう。
examples.english: Spring breezes feel nice, so let's open the window and let the air into the room.

notes:
{風|かぜ} refers to the natural movement of air. Don't confuse with {風邪|かぜ} (a cold/flu)—same pronunciation but different meaning and kanji.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}く (the wind blows)
- {風|かぜ}が{強|つよ}い/{弱|よわ}い (the wind is strong/weak)
- {風|かぜ}が{止|と}む (the wind stops)
- {風|かぜ}に{乗|の}る (to ride the wind)
- {風|かぜ}を{切|き}る (to cut through the wind)

TYPES OF WIND:
- {強風|きょうふう} (strong wind)
- {微風|びふう} (gentle breeze)
- {向|む}かい{風|かぜ} (headwind)
- {追|お}い{風|かぜ} (tailwind)
- {春風|はるかぜ} (spring breeze)

RELATED WORDS:
- {台風|たいふう} (typhoon)
- {風向|かざむ}き (wind direction)
- そよ{風|かぜ} (gentle breeze)
